summary: Built SC-021 as designed. The new `comments.Block`, `Unblock` and `Blocked` store lives in `block.go`. Post, Cast, Withdraw and Send each refuse a blocked account inside their own single statement, and a follow-up read picks the 403. The owner gets block, unblock and `/admin/blocked` routes, an `admin_blocked.html` page, a Block form on the moderation list and a 'blocked' badge on feedback. The full suite `go test -count=1 -p 4 ./...` passes. Both E-006 finish-line bodies (read from the ledger, run in a scratch copy of this tree) exit 0 against the real built binary.

obligations.how: Built the whole SC-021 shape list and fed every shape in by tests. Route and store shapes are in TestBlock and TestBlockStore; refusals in TestBlockedRefusals; the page in TestBlockedPage; restore in TestUnblockRestores; matrix, dislike and feedback noninterference through ownerRouteStatus and observe(). Both E-006 finish-line bodies exit 0 against the built binary.

Each not-removed comment on the Blocked users page has a details.remove two-step posting to /admin/comments/<id>/remove with hidden from=blocked. adminCommentRemove has from=blocked as a first-class case that lands on /admin/blocked whatever the report's state. bodyRow now carries a landing string with from=blocked rows (urlencoded, alias, multipart; 'Blocked', admin+blocked and repeated are 400). TestCommentRemove has landing rows for published, unpublished and draft reports. TestUnblockRestores presses the real remove forms while blocked, then the real Unblock form.

modItem.ParentRemoved is now ParentHidden; admin_report.html says 'in reply to a hidden comment'; the two remove_test.go expectations are updated. TestBlockControls checks a reply under a blocked parent says 'hidden' and not 'removed'.

obligations.how: Followed the critic's version. comments.New(db, now, ownerID) binds the owner id at router.go from cfg.OwnerGitHubID. Block returns ErrOwnerBlock for that id and fails closed with an error (not ErrOwnerBlock) when ownerID <= 0. The handler maps ErrOwnerBlock to 400. TestBlockStore asserts the store-level refusals (owner, no owner pinned, non-account ids); TestBlock asserts the 400 through the route.

Each of Post, Cast, Withdraw and Send returns a wrapped error (for example 'votes: withdraw: is blocked: %w') when the follow-up read fails. Each Book has an unexported isBlocked seam, replaced in the package's own tests: TestPostBlockReadFails, TestBlockedReadFails, TestSendBlockReadFails assert a wrapped non-sentinel error, and for Withdraw never nil. The server-level TestBlockedReadFault swaps blocked_accounts for a view that errors on evaluation and asserts a 503 with nothing stored on all routes. A temporary mutation confirmed the withdraw and reply-to-missing rows reach the follow-up read.

tests.command: real binary driven through the acceptance harness (a scratch script on the scratch copy): reader and bad-actor comment, vote and send feedback; the owner presses the Block form; then I read /admin/blocked, the admin report page and the public page
tests.note: The moderation list shows closed Block and Remove two-steps. After the block the owner lands on /admin/blocked#blocked-8102, which lists the comment with a /reports/alpha#comment-1 parent link, the feedback and an Unblock form. The feedback article carries the 'blocked' badge. The blocked account's new comment gets 403 'Your account cannot take part here.' A visitor sees no trace of the comment or the login, and the count reads '1 comment'.

deviations: Block's owner refusal is in the store, not in the handler as design 229 said: comments.New takes the owner id, Block returns ErrOwnerBlock and fails closed when no owner is pinned (decided findings m2 and its critic note). The handler only maps ErrOwnerBlock to 400.
Each Book (comments, votes, feedback) has an unexported isBlocked seam so the follow-up-read failure can be tested (finding m3's critic note). The design had a plain read.

The Blocked users page builds parent links through a.tree, Find and branchRoot, one read per published report that has a reply on the page, and prints 'in reply to a hidden comment' as text when the parent is drawn nowhere (finding m5's critic note). The design used a fixed /reports/<slug>#comment-<parent>.

A blocked account's feedback is listed with a link to /admin/reports/<slug>#feedback-<id>, where the author reads and answers it, rather than the reader page. SenderMessage and BlockedComment also carry Published, which the design's types lacked, so an unpublished report links to its admin page.

Block and unblock take no field, and their handlers never read the body (lesson #973's 'decided choice to ignore the body'). They are classified 'no field' in TestPostRoutesAreClassified, and TestBlock sends every removeBodyRows shape to both.
from=blocked is checked first in adminCommentRemove, so it lands on /admin/blocked for drafts and unpublished reports too (M1's critic note). bodyRow's landing went from a bool to a string.

The comments-package tests are named TestBlockStore, TestPostRefusesBlocked and so on, not TestBlock, because TestBlock names the server route test in the design. No workaround for an outside defect was needed, so there is no setting or notice.
not_built: No screens are declared. The Blocked users page and the admin report page sit behind GitHub sign-in, and config refuses to start without HBAND_* variables (lesson #961), so the engine cannot open them with a bare command. They were rendered and read through the real binary over HTTP instead, but not in a real browser (m9 was deferred by a person).
Not built, as decided: a Block entry point on feedback articles (m8), a size bound on the Blocked users page (m10), and a census of public write routes (m7). All three were deferred by decision.
follow_ups: Architecture globs: C-009 should own internal/server/templates/admin_blocked.html and admin_report.html, and C-005 or C-009 the new server tests (block_test.go, unblock_test.go). I could not file this as a paths edit because the record edits are capped at three.
tests/acceptance/check_e006_1_stops_at_block.py is scaffolding that now reports 'passes outright'. Lesson #976 says it should go; its own docstring says it need not, so I left it.

A blocked reader is still shown the comment, vote and feedback forms (reader pages must stay byte-identical, #950) and gets a bare 403 text page when it presses one. Decide whether a friendlier notice is wanted.

A signed-in Chrome render of /admin/blocked and the moderation list (m9), and the owner-page size bound (m10): /admin/blocked also does one feedback query per account and one thread read per published report with replies.
Run the engine's Fitness op=check on .taad/fitness.yaml; I had no such tool and relied on go test ./internal/fitnessrules plus a manual single-quote count.
